subject: Private VPC pricing — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC pricing — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps: \n
Recap:\n- FintechCo is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for production inference across two environments (staging + prod) with strict data residency requirements.\n- Primary workloads: realtime chat assistants (low-latency) + nightly batch embedding jobs.\n- Preliminary monthly token estimate: you mentioned ~120M tokens/month for chat + ~80M tokens/month for embeddings (200M total).\n\nOpen items we discussed that will affect pricing:\n1) Token volumes and seasonality: please confirm expected range (typical / peak) for both realtime and batch.\n2) Budget target: you said leadership is thinking about a $/1M-tokens target — can you share a target $/1M tokens or monthly budget range we should design toward?\n3) Environments: confirm exact environment count (dev, qa, staging, prod). Licensing and support tiers scale by environment count.\n4) Support & SLA: confirm if you require business-hours vs 24x7 escalation and if a managed onboarding SOW is needed.\n\nWhat I’m attaching: draft pricing worksheet (redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx) that maps unit economics for common licensing options (capacity-based vs instance-license + per-token unit).\n\nProposed next steps:\n- You: confirm token volume ranges (typical + peak) and a target $/1M tokens or monthly budget range.\n- Us: I’ll send a short pricing estimate (pdf) that shows 2 licensing options and support tiers for 2 vs 4 environments.\n- If numbers look good, we can schedule a 30-min procurement call with Marissa next week to walk the licensing and contract flow.\n\nThanks —\nBen\nBen Carter\nAccount Executive, Redwood Inference\nben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123\nRedwood Inference\n\nAttachment: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC pricing — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Ben — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: \n\nToken volumes:\n- Chat (realtime): baseline 120M tokens/mo, peak 240M tokens/mo during promotions (factor ~2).\n- Embeddings (batch): baseline 80M tokens/mo, peaks up to 150M tokens/mo for monthly re-index jobs.\n- Aggregate typical: ~200M tokens/mo, aggregate peak ~390M tokens/mo.\n\nBudget target:\n- We don’t have a firm $/1M target yet. Leadership gave a ballpark monthly budget of $8k–$20k depending on the licensing model and support.\n\nEnvironments:\n- We need staging + prod (2). Dev will be handled in shared infra for now, QA is optional. If pricing for an additional environment looks reasonable, we may add later.\n\nSupport/SLA:\n- Business-hours support is acceptable initially. We’ll want a path to 24x7 once in prod. Managed onboarding SOW likely required (security review + playbook).\n\nNext: please share the estimate and two licensing options. Also include notes on what’s in the managed onboarding SOW and expected timeline.\n\n—Alex\nAlex Johnson\nVP Product, FintechCo\nalex.johnson@fintechco.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC pricing — follow-up and next steps

Alex — great, thanks for the specifics. Based on the numbers you shared (typical 200M / peak ~390M tokens), I attached a short estimate with two recommended licensing approaches and the unit economics per 1M tokens. High level: \n\nOption A — Capacity license (recommended for predictable throughput):\n- Fixed monthly capacity commitment that covers up to a defined number of concurrent requests and baseline token volume.\n- Unit economics (from attached): $1,800–$2,400 per 1M tokens effective at 200M tokens/mo depending on GPU size and batching assumptions.\n- Pros: predictable latency/SLA, lower tail latency during peaks, simpler OPEX.\n- Cons: higher committed spend if volume is lower than baseline.\n\nOption B — Hybrid license (license + per-token overage):\n- Per-environment license fee (covers the control plane + reserved infra) + $/1M tokens for inference.\n- Unit economics: $2,500–$3,200 per 1M tokens at 200M tokens/mo, with volume discounts kicking in above 300M/mo.\n- Pros: lower base commitment, easier to start smaller.\n\nEnvironments & Support:\n- Pricing worksheet models 2 environments (staging + prod) and an add-on price for each additional environment.\n- Business-hours support included in base; 24x7 is an add-on with guaranteed response SLAs and a dedicated escalation path.\n- Managed onboarding SOW typically priced as a one-time professional services fee (3–6 weeks) covering security onboarding, network setup, and performance tuning. Details in the attached estimate.\n\nNext steps I propose:\n1) Marissa and I finalize a formal estimate (pdf) and SOW draft — I attached the first draft (redwood-private-pricing-estimate.pdf).\n2) If the estimate falls within your $8k–$20k band for the first phase, we schedule a procurement/contract call to review T&C and timelines.\n3) We can set an optional 2-week pilot to validate infra and performance before committing to a larger capacity license.\n\nMarissa — can you please take point on the procurement call scheduling and confirm typical PS SOW timeline and cost ranges we should propose?\n\nBen\nBen Carter\nAccount Executive, Redwood Inference\n\nAttachment: redwood-private-pricing-estimate.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private VPC pricing — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex — looping in procurement and PS as discussed. Quick notes on SOW and timelines: \n\n- Typical PS SOW (managed onboarding): 3–6 weeks, team includes solutions engineer + security engineer + project manager. Estimated one-time fee: $45k–$75k depending on environment complexity and SOC2 evidence collection.\n- Pilot option: 2 weeks of validation (smaller environment) — estimated $8k–$12k for engineering time if you’d like Redwood-managed pilot.\n- Contracting: we can do a standard SLA with an enterprise addendum (data residency + logging/audit) and include a 90-day performance review.\n\nIf the $8k–$20k monthly band is accurate for the first year, Option A (capacity) at the lower unit economics would likely be within range only if we size the capacity conservatively with a flexible overage buffer. Option B is easier to start under the lower monthly budget but scales in unit cost.\n\nPlease suggest 2x 30-min time slots for next week for a procurement + legal intro call.\n\nThanks —\nMarissa Cole\nSr. Sales Ops, Redwood Inference\nmarissa.cole@redwood.com
